first_week.eligible_universe: all Mondays from 2024-01-01 through 2025-11-24 excluding previously used candidate-02 weeks
first_week.selection_method: Python random.Random(seed).choice over chronologically sorted eligible Mondays

level_registry: each completed four-hour high and low, valid for 24 hours
each completed eight-hour high and low, valid for 48 hours
each previous completed UTC-day high and low, valid for 72 hours
locked_hypothesis.one_use_rule: an underlying structural level is consumed at its first qualifying breach and cannot create a second event
locked_hypothesis.near_duplicate_rule: levels breached in the same minute within 0.10 prior ATR are treated as one liquidity cluster
locked_hypothesis.acceptance: at least two closes remain beyond the level in the three-minute classification window, basis-adjusted spot also crosses, spot acceptance is at least 25% of perpetual acceptance, and basis expansion contributes at most 75%
locked_hypothesis.delivery_confirmation: same-direction displacement closes beyond the level, leaves a causal three-candle FVG, and a later completed-minute retest touches the gap while closing beyond both its midpoint and the old level
locked_hypothesis.invalidation: a retest that trades 0.10 prior ATR back inside the old level invalidates acceptance
locked_hypothesis.objective: nearest intact pre-event five-minute external pivot with cost-after reward/risk at least 1.10
locked_hypothesis.ambiguous_state: no trade when price, spot participation, basis, displacement, retest or target state is incomplete

promotion_rule: The central all-level portfolio and at least one adjacent horizon must pass every original weekly gate, central signals must involve at least two structural source categories, and no active source component may have negative after-cost expectancy. Otherwise run one core-variable ablation on the revealed week before discarding.

research_basis.reference: Osler, Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets
research_basis.implication: prior structural highs and lows are plausible stop-liquidity clocks but a breach alone is not directional evidence

research_basis.reference: Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov, The Price Impact of Order Book Events
research_basis.implication: turnover-qualified order-flow events must be interpreted relative to available liquidity

research_basis.reference: Xu et al., Limit-order book resiliency after effective market orders
research_basis.implication: post-shock price acceptance and replenishment distinguish resilience from continuation

research_basis.reference: Hansen, Kim and Kimbrough, Periodicity in Cryptocurrency Volatility and Liquidity
research_basis.implication: fixed completed four-hour, eight-hour and UTC-day ranges provide prospective recurring market clocks
